answers: The opposition party questioned about sending military groups to provinces in order to fix long-term care. The Prime Minister answered that the government needed to make sure seniors across the country were properly cared for, and they sent in the military to help the provinces. The opposition party also questioned about applying the national standards so that long-term care was governed by the same principles as the Canada Health Act. The Prime Minister elaborated that due the Covid-19, pushing the project had become extremely difficult.

full.prediction: The debate over the situation of long-term care centered on the poor conditions and neglect in facilities, as highlighted by the Canadian Armed Forces' report. Critics, including members of the opposition and the NDP, called for federal leadership, national standards, and an end to profit-driven models in long-term care. The government defended its efforts to support provinces and territories, emphasizing collaboration and the need for systemic reform, but faced accusations of inaction and prioritizing political interests over the well-being of seniors.
